ds: Smuggling, counterfeit and illegal manufacture of tobacco and other excise goods to avoid duty, including diversion from duty suspension, undeclared transit and sale through informal retail. Cash proceeds are layered via small shops, wholesalers and cross-border transfers.

src.t: WHO FCTC, Protocol to Eliminate Illicit Trade in Tobacco Products (2012)
OECD and EUIPO, public material on illicit trade
World Customs Organization, public material on tobacco smuggling

cn.rt: Retail cash proceeds of illicit tobacco deposited via everyday accounts at branch; trade and merchant elements are out of consumer scope.

rat: Cash-heavy retailers and wholesalers, cash deposits and supplier remittances.

ind.n: Wholesaler purchases far exceed local market demand
ind.cx: Volumes of cigarettes or alcohol bought by a retailer or distributor exceed plausible consumption.
ind.fp: Border areas and tourism cause higher sales.
ind.ds: Volumes of cigarettes or alcohol bought by a retailer or distributor exceed plausible consumption.

ind.n: Goods in transit declared to low-tax or non-EU destinations but not arriving
ind.cx: Duty-suspended shipments disappear or end up in domestic markets.
ind.ds: Duty-suspended shipments disappear or end up in domestic markets.

ind.n: Cash-heavy small shops with large tobacco turnover and little card use
ind.cx: Convenience stores with cash deposits not matching stock purchases.
ind.ds: Customer's business relies heavily on cash receipts, making revenue difficult to verify against stock, costs or card use.

ind.n: Payments to or from free-trade zones and tax-free ports
ind.cx: Transfers linked to zones known for tobacco diversion.
ind.ds: Transfers linked to zones known for tobacco diversion.

ind.n: Counterfeit or unbranded cigarettes sold with 'cheap' pricing
ind.fp: Promotions exist but not below duty.
ind.ds: Prices are implausibly low for authentic or duty-paid products, suggesting counterfeit or illicit supply.
ind.cn: Branded or duty-paid goods priced far below genuine market levels

ind.n: Illegal factory equipment or leaf purchases
ind.cx: Orders for tobacco-making machinery, paper, filters.
ind.ds: Orders for tobacco-making machinery, paper, filters.

ind.n: Cross-border cash and remittance flows from retailers to overseas suppliers
ind.cx: Regular remittances to suppliers in source countries without invoices.
ind.ds: Regular remittances to suppliers in source countries without invoices.

ind.n: Vehicle or container rental by small firms for bulk transport
ind.cx: Frequent rental or purchase of vans and containers.
ind.ds: Frequent rental or purchase of vans and containers.

ctl.ds: Risk-based vetting of intermediaries, brokers, partners and suppliers covering ownership, experience, references, public-official links and selection rationale. It limits exposure through proxies.

Compares reported volumes with capacity, production, mass balance, concession size and national trade statistics to test whether quantities are physically possible. It exposes inflated, laundered or mislabelled flows.

Verifies that goods physically moved as documented by matching shipping, container, customs and logistics records, and by requesting transport evidence such as delivery confirmations and warehouse records for sampled trades. It exposes fictitious or misdescribed shipments used to justify payments.

ctl.n: Trade document review and consistency checking
ctl.ds: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.

Reconciles trade documents, invoices and shipments with the payments that settle them and reviews settlement made outside standard banking channels. It exposes trade-based laundering where payment logic does not match the underlying deal.
Reconciles cash, stock purchases, sales and exports with declared business activity to test whether deposits are plausible. It is used to identify unrecorded or injected cash.

Applies targeted enhanced checks to customer types or sectors known to be vulnerable to misuse, such as cash-intensive trades, money service businesses, high-value dealers, professional services, charities or waste handlers. Questions and evidence are tailored to how the sector normally operates.

Applies enhanced checks to operators, counterparties, storage rationale and transactions that involve free-trade zones and free ports, including facility operator controls. It addresses the opacity and reduced oversight these locations can offer.

Compares declared unit prices, award values, fees and ancillary costs with reference databases, estimates and comparable contracts, and requires documented rationale for outliers. It detects over- and under-invoicing and inflated awards.

Educates retailers, suppliers, hospitality providers and other partners to recognise and report suspicious patterns, and invites reporting channels. It extends detection to people who see activity before the institution does.

Requires end-user statements, authenticates their signatories, verifies licences and sites, and obtains post-delivery reports for goods and funds. It confirms that goods or funds reach the stated end use.

Provides protected, confidential channels for staff, workers and suppliers to report misconduct or concerns, together with conduct monitoring to surface insider collusion. It brings internal and supply-chain issues to light.
Participates in sector, regulator and public-private forums and platform cooperation to receive and share typologies and indicators where lawful. It keeps scenarios current.
